A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExPLoRA study and contain 20 pages, including Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, 19 tables and nine figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original ExPLoRA experiments, ablations and representation analyses in Sections 6–7 and Appendix B, including satellite-image, WILDS and VisDA-2017 results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results and analyses, including fMoW-RGB evaluations and the VisDA-2017 initialization experiments.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same selective block unfreezing, Q/V LoRA updates, normalization training, MAE/DinoV2 objectives and downstream adaptation procedures.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is unchanged across Section 6 and Appendix B: RGB, multispectral and temporal satellite imagery, medical and wildlife classification, agricultural detection, and VisDA-2017 synthetic-to-real adaptation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments. This includes the PEFT comparisons in Tables 1 and 16 and the CDTrans, PMTrans, TVT and SSRT comparisons in Table 17.

E3.justification: Sections 6 and Appendices B–C retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training budgets and testing procedures. Table 18's dataset sizes and recommended pre-training iterations also match.

E4.justification: The block/rank/normalization ablations, representation analyses, compute and convergence studies, decoder-rank and backbone-size experiments, and attention-map cases are unchanged in Section 7 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: Matched results are identical, including 79.28% fMoW-RGB accuracy in Table 1, 77.48% linear-probing accuracy in Table 2, and 90.9% VisDA-2017 accuracy for SSRT with ExPLoRA initialization in Table 17. Appendix results, plotted findings and carbon estimates are also retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the domain and parameter-space definitions in Sections 3–5, and the UDA assumptions in Appendix A.2 are mathematically unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion preserve the same contributions and claims about efficient extended pre-training, domain adaptation, accuracy and computational savings.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including the layer-information explanation in Section 7, possible iWildcam overfitting in Section 6.2, and limited benefits on small datasets in Appendix C.5.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training schedules and code/data access information are retained. Appendix C.1 corrects 'NVIDA' to 'NVIDIA', but this does not change the identified GPU or provide new technical information.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A and the 80-item bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to PEFT, geospatial adaptation and unsupervised domain adaptation.

P1.justification: v5 expands the running title, replaces 'appendix' with 'section' in cross-references, and makes small spelling and hyphenation corrections. Section order and substantive prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded running header and small typesetting and line-wrapping adjustments change page presentation slightly. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–19 retain their displays, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v5 makes small editorial and presentation corrections while preserving the same method, empirical evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendices. These cosmetic adjustments do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
